The '''2019–20 Eredivisie''' was the 64th season of the Dutch football league [[Eredivisie]] since its establishment in 1955. The season began on 2 August 2019 and was suspended on 12 March 2020 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]. The season was abandoned on 24 April.<ref name=suspended/><ref name="coronavirusSeason">{{cite news|url=https://nos.nl/artikel/2331612-knvb-beslist-ajax-nummer-een-geen-promotie-degradatie.html|title=KNVB beslist: Ajax nummer één, geen promotie/degradatie|trans-title=KNVB decides: Ajax number one, no promotion/relegation|publisher=[[Nederlandse Omroep Stichting|NOS]]|language=nl|date=24 April 2020|access-date=24 April 2020}}</ref>

[[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] were the defending champion. [[FC Twente|Twente]], [[RKC Waalwijk]], and [[Sparta Rotterdam]] joined as the promoted clubs from the [[2018–19 Eerste Divisie]]. They replaced [[NAC Breda]], [[SBV Excelsior|Excelsior]], and [[De Graafschap]] who were relegated to the [[2019–20 Eerste Divisie]].

== Effects of the COVID-19 pandemic ==
On 12 March 2020, all football leagues were suspended until 31 March as the Dutch government prohibited events due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]].<ref name=suspended>{{cite web|url=https://www.knvb.nl/nieuws/amateurvoetbal/uitgelicht/59620/tot-en-met-31-maart-geen-voetbal-nederland|title=tot en met 31 maart geen voetbal in nederland|trans-title=Until 31 March no football in the Netherlands|publisher=KNVB|language=nl|date=12 March 2020|access-date=19 March 2020}}</ref> On 15 March this period was extended until 6 April.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.knvb.nl/nieuws/amateurvoetbal/competitiezaken/59633/geen-voetbalwedstrijden-tot-en-met-6-april|title=Geen voetbalwedstrijden tot en met 6 april|trans-title=No football matches until 6 April|publisher=KNVB|language=nl|date=15 March 2020|access-date=19 March 2020}}</ref> Following the decision of the Dutch government to prohibit all gatherings and events until 1 June 2020, this period was further extended.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.voetbal247.nl/voetbalseizoen-lijkt-ten-einde-kabinet-verlengt-sluiting-tot-1-juni/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200329232232/https://www.voetbal247.nl/voetbalseizoen-lijkt-ten-einde-kabinet-verlengt-sluiting-tot-1-juni/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=March 29, 2020|title=Voetbalseizoen lijkt ten einde: Kabinet verlengt maatregelen tot 1 juni|trans-title=Football season seems to have ended: Government extends measures until 1 June 2020|publisher=voetbal247.nl|language=nl|date=23 March 2020|access-date=30 March 2020}}</ref>

On 2 April, several clubs, including [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]], [[AZ Alkmaar|AZ]] and [[PSV Eindhoven|PSV]], indicated they were not willing to play the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nos.nl/l/2329205|title=Topclubs willen niet verder, Eredivisie CV wil dinsdag pas beslissen|trans-title=Top clubs do not want to continue, Eredivisie CV wants to decide Tuesday|language=nl|publisher=[[Nederlandse Omroep Stichting|NOS]]|date=2 April 2020|access-date=2 April 2020}}</ref>

The Dutch government announced on 21 April that all events subject to authorization would remain prohibited until at least 1 September 2020. As a result, the [[Royal Dutch Football Association|KNVB]] announced on the same day that it did not intend to resume the 2019–20 season. A final decision would be taken after consultation with the [[UEFA]] and debating the consequences with the clubs involved.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.knvb.nl/nieuws/betaald-voetbal/eredivisie/59877/status-betaaldvoetbalcompetities-naar-aanleiding-van-update|title=Status betaaldvoetbalcompetities naar aanleiding van update maatregelen overheid|trans-title=Status professional football in response to the update measures of the government.|publisher=KNVB|language=nl|date=21 April 2020|access-date=22 April 2020}}</ref>

On 24 April 2020 the KNVB announced their final decision:<ref name="coronavirusSeason"/>
* The ranking on 8 March 2020 is the final ranking, but [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] will not be champions.
* There will be no promotion nor relegation between the Eredivisie and Eerste Divisie.
* European places will be assigned based on the ranking on 8 March: [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] for [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] and [[AZ Alkmaar|AZ]], and [[2020–21 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] for [[Feyenoord]], [[PSV Eindhoven|PSV]], and [[Willem II Tilburg|Willem II]].

The KNVB had intended to resume the season on 19 June [[behind closed doors (sports)|behind closed doors]], but announced in a statement that the government's decision to ban all public events until September made it impossible to finish the season on time.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11906/11978351/ajax-denied-title-as-dutch-eredivisie-season-declared-void-european-places-decided-no-relegation |title=Ajax denied title as Dutch Eredivisie season declared void, European places decided, no relegation |publisher=Sky Sports  |date=25 April 2020 |access-date=26 April 2020}}</ref>

AZ only played their first home game at [[AFAS Stadion]] due to the stadium's roof collapse on 10 August 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rtlnieuws.nl/nieuws/artikel/4809756/dak-az-stadion-ingestort |title=Dak van AZ-stadion gedeeltelijk ingestort |date=10 August 2019 |website=RTL Nieuws |access-date=10 August 2019 |language=nl }}</ref> From then on they've played their home matches at the 17,000-capacity [[Cars Jeans Stadion]] in [[The Hague]], home of [[ADO Den Haag]]. AZ returned to their 'roofless' AFAS Stadion for the match against Ajax on 15 December 2019.
